explanation: There is no cultural taboo in the UK against eating or handling food with the left hand. British table manners focus on using the knife and fork correctly: fork in the left hand and knife in the right while cutting, then either keeping the fork in the left hand ('Continental' style) or switching it to the right hand to eat ('American' style) - both are acceptable, and the choice of hand carries no stigma.
local_tip: Hold your fork in your left hand and knife in your right when cutting; either keep the fork in your left hand to eat or switch it to your right - both styles are normal in the UK.

also_check.note: The left hand is traditionally considered unclean for eating; the right hand is used for handling and eating food.
Eating or passing food with the left hand is discouraged; the right hand is used for eating and greeting.
There is no hand taboo; chopsticks are used with either hand and left-handedness carries no stigma.
